summary: Conservation is the core pledge: Lebanon aims to protect at least 20% of natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems while representing all ecosystem types in the protected-area network, ensure nature reserves reach at least 5% of the country—about 512.25 km² of the reported land area—and sustainably manage 50% of natural ecosystems in spatial planning. It also commits to identifying the status of 75% of known flora and fauna species and implementing conservation actions for 50% of threatened species. Restoration focuses on rehabilitating at least 20% of degraded sites to sustain ecosystem services. These broad ambitions are notable where forest covers only 2.3% of Lebanon and grassland 0.1%; however, no degraded-site baseline is provided for translating the restoration goal into an area.
